title: Render empty slice metadata without broken emphasis
lead: A slice with no size renders its header as `**Size: **`, which is not valid bold in CommonMark, so the asterisks appear literally.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: `slice_header` (`src/slicer/render.py:72`) builds `**Size: {sl.size}**`. When `size` is empty the closing `**` follows a space, so it is not right-flanking and does not close the emphasis; renderers show the literal `**Size: **`. Every current open slice (S126-S131) has an empty size, so the defect shows in the rendered slices under `.slicer/render/slices/`. `Findings` and `Tree` use `**Label:** value` and are not affected; only `Size` puts the value inside the bold. This is cosmetic and does not affect state or `check`.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/render.py` (`slice_header`)
- the render tests that pin the header bytes

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. A slice with an empty size renders a header whose bold spans are valid CommonMark (no `** ` before a closing `**`).
2. A slice with a size still renders the size legibly.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: Use **Size:** M, with the value outside the bold like Findings and Tree. Keep **Size:** when the size is empty. The owner approved this format and implementation now; regenerate all affected slice files.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: Header renders validly with and without a size; suite and `slicer check` pass.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit, including the re-rendered slices.
